title: EPIC 1: Core Architecture & Execution Environment
description: Build a stable modular application that behaves correctly when packaged as a PyInstaller onefile executable. Modules: UI orchestration, Google Maps scraping, website scraping, data normalization, Excel generation, licensing & enforcement.

title: Story 1.1 – Project Structure & Responsibilities
description: Define strict module boundaries (UI orchestration, Google Maps scraping, website scraping, data normalization, Excel generation, licensing & enforcement). Keep UI thin, prevent scrapers from touching UI state, and ensure modules are importable in frozen mode.

title: Story 1.2 – EXE-Safe Path & Runtime Detection
description: Detect frozen execution (sys.frozen), define a single BASE_DIR resolver, route all file operations through a centralized path utility, and create logs/output/license directories at runtime.

title: Story 1.3 – Logging Infrastructure
description: Implement structured logging that persists across runs and writes to disk, including timestamp, app version, machine fingerprint (hashed), license status, and enforcement actions.

title: Improve Streamlit UI for new vs existing lead files
description:
Enhance Streamlit app UX so users can clearly choose between starting a new lead scrape (new query) and appending to an existing Excel file. The UI should:
- Make the two modes obvious and self-explanatory from the sidebar
- Allow providing an existing file path or uploading a file for append mode
- Show clear progress feedback during scraping (status text + progress bar)
- Clearly indicate where results are saved and whether they were appended or newly created.

title: EPIC 6: Streamlit UI & Interaction Model
description: Provide a stable, desktop-friendly Streamlit UI for inputs, progress feedback, and results display.

title: Story 6.1 – User Inputs
description: Provide Streamlit inputs for search query, optional result limit, and optional output directory, with validation before starting scraping.

title: Story 6.2 – Progress & Feedback
description: Show progress status and messages for each major phase (search, scroll, scrape), log each phase, and display non-blocking warnings without freezing the UI.

title: Story 6.3 – Results Display
description: Display scraped data in a table with clickable links, limit rows for performance if needed, and show license-related warnings where applicable.

title: EPIC 4: Data Normalization & Validation
description: Ensure output data is consistent, deduplicated, and clean, suitable for Excel export and analysis.

title: Story 4.1 – Canonical Data Model
description: Define a fixed column schema, ensure one row per business, convert list fields to strings, and normalize empty values.

title: Story 4.2 – Deduplication & Cleanup
description: Deduplicate rows by website or (business name + address), normalize phone numbers, trim whitespace, and sanitize strings for Excel.

title: EPIC 2: Google Maps Scraping Engine
description: Extract business listings reliably from Google Maps: query execution, result discovery & scrolling, business data extraction.

title: Story 2.1 – Query Execution
description: Accept user query input, open Google Maps, submit the query, wait for the results panel, and retry safely on slow loads.

title: Story 2.2 – Results Discovery & Scrolling
description: Detect the results container, scroll until the result limit is reached or no new listings load, track already-seen listings, and enforce a dynamic result cap (licensing-aware).

title: Story 2.3 – Business Data Extraction
description: Extract business name, address, phone, website, rating, review count; handle missing fields gracefully and normalize values.

title: EPIC 3: Website & Social Data Extraction
description: Extract additional lead data (social links, emails, WhatsApp) from business websites linked from Google Maps.

title: Story 3.1 – Website Navigation
description: Validate website URLs, handle redirects, apply request timeouts, and abort safely on failures while scraping business websites.

title: Story 3.2 – Social Media & Contact Extraction
description: Extract social media links (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Twitter/X), emails, and WhatsApp links from business websites; deduplicate results and restrict crawling to homepage only.

title: EPIC 8: Logging, Auditing & Feedback Loop
description: Enable runtime logging and offline license issuance workflow via log exchange with the developer.

title: Story 8.1 – Runtime Logging
description: Log app start, machine fingerprint hash, license validation results, scraping attempts, and enforcement triggers; persist logs to disk.

title: Story 8.2 – License Issuance Workflow
description: Document and support a workflow where the user runs without license, sends logs, developer generates license based on fingerprint, and user installs license locally.

title: EPIC 5: Excel Output & Persistence
description: Generate reliable Excel files with hyperlinks and EXE-safe persistence before download.

title: Story 5.1 – Excel Writer Module
description: Write DataFrames to .xlsx with clickable hyperlinks, reasonable column widths, and support for large datasets.

title: Story 5.2 – EXE-Safe Download Strategy
description: Persist Excel files to disk before UI download, track file paths in session state, and ensure reruns do not delete or lose references to files.

title: EPIC 9: Packaging & Distribution
description: Deliver a professional standalone executable via PyInstaller (and optionally Streamlit Desktop), validated on Windows and macOS.

title: Story 9.1 – PyInstaller Configuration
description: Configure PyInstaller with hidden imports and data directories, validate Selenium in frozen mode, and keep bundle size reasonable.

title: Story 9.2 – Cross-Platform Validation
description: Validate Windows and macOS execution, including path permissions, ChromeDriver behavior, and license persistence across restarts.

title: Duplicate log entries in Streamlit app
description:
The Streamlit-based UI currently writes multiple identical log lines for single user actions (e.g., workflow mode selection, file uploads, and Start Scraping clicks). This makes  noisy and harder to inspect when users send logs for support, as seen in recent runs where each event appears 4–6 times.

Acceptance criteria:
- Each logical user action (mode change, Start Scraping click, file upload, existing file load, save) should result in at most one log line per run, or a clearly grouped set for a single scrape run.
- Ensure Streamlit reruns do not cause duplicated log records for the same interaction.
- Keep the logging verbose enough for support (queries, paths, row counts, errors) but deduplicated and easy to read.
- Confirm behavior both in dev (Python script) and in the packaged Windows .exe.

title: EPIC 10: Documentation & Handoff
description: Produce internal and user-facing documentation for licensing, usage, failure modes, and rebuild process.

title: Story 10.1 – Internal Engineering Docs
description: Document licensing flow, enforcement logic, failure modes, and rebuild process for developers.

title: Story 10.2 – User-Facing Instructions
description: Document how to run the app, generate leads, install a license, and what happens when the license expires.

title: Add file-based logging for shipped executable
description:
Add robust file-based logging for the packaged Windows .exe so end users can send log files when they encounter issues. Requirements:
- Log to a user-writable directory (alongside output files), with a dedicated logs folder.
- Capture high-level app events, start/stop, and scraping steps.
- Capture errors and stack traces from both the Streamlit UI and CLI flows.
- Use rotation or size limits to prevent unbounded log growth.
- Ensure logging works correctly when running as a PyInstaller-frozen executable on Windows.

title: EPIC 7: Licensing & Enforcement System
description: Implement an offline, machine-bound, time-limited licensing system with enforcement rules.

title: Story 7.1 – Machine Fingerprint Generation
description: Generate a hashed machine fingerprint (e.g., from MAC address), never expose raw MAC in UI, and log only the hash.

title: Story 7.2 – License Data Model
description: Define a non-human-readable license schema with fingerprint, expiry date, max results per run, and optional feature flags.

title: Story 7.3 – License Key Encoding (Offline)
description: Implement a separate offline script to encode license data into an opaque key using symmetric encryption or signed payloads.

title: Story 7.4 – License Key Storage
description: Load license keys from file or user input, store them locally without decoding to plaintext, and validate on app startup.

title: Story 7.5 – License Validation Logic
description: Decode license keys internally, validate fingerprint, expiry, and result limits, and fail gracefully if invalid.

title: Story 7.6 – Enforcement Rules
description: Enforce limits for missing/invalid/expired licenses (result caps, export restrictions, preview-only mode), and log all enforcement actions.
